Name: HDCore (Honest Display Core)
Author: ParadoxQED
Description:
[b]Description[/b]
The HD in HDCore also stands for [b]Honest Display[/b]: the icons and the stats panel are the Display; the calibrated prices and the un-fudged totals are the Honest.
HDCore does five jobs.
[b]HD item icons.[/b] Vanilla draws every item icon from a hard-coded 16×16 slice of its texture and then scales that slice 4×, so a 64×64 texture only ever shows its top-left corner. HDCore samples the whole texture and scales it by "64 / source edge": the icon still fills exactly one 64px grid cell, but carries four times the linear detail. 16×16 art looks identical to vanilla, 64×64 art is sharp, and the two can sit side by side without one looking blurry.
[b]An always-on stats panel.[/b] Health, stamina, defense, immunity, speed, damage, crit chance, weapon speed and fishing, drawn in a compact panel you can toggle, drag and scale. It reads the totals the game has already computed, so vanilla boots, rings, cooked food, festival dishes and any mod that writes its bonuses into the game's buff effects are all counted automatically. No registration, no per-mod patch, no setup.
[b]Auto-pricing (3.0.0).[/b] Content mods can register their items and the engine prices them the way vanilla does: sell value = data price (quality and profession bonuses still apply on top), shop price = 2× data price, recipes = 1/10 of the target's shop price, weapons = vanilla level formula × 100. Food is priced by a calibrated category coefficient (fish, milk, egg, artisan, vegetable, fruit, forage, flower, dish) plus a per-point bonus for food buffs; accessories and armor are summed from vanilla-equivalent stat dimensions and snapped to the vanilla ring price ladder. The calibration comes from regression on vanilla pricing data — modded food stops being priced by guesswork and modded rings stop being priced arbitrarily. Nothing changes unless a mod registers: with no registration, the pricing engine is entirely inert, and categories outside the calibrated list are refused outright (those items keep their original prices).
[b]Tooltip icon rows (3.2.0).[/b] Vanilla reserves a strip at the bottom of an item's tooltip for "special icon" rows — a small picture plus one line of text — and uses it for weapon enchantments. HDCore opens that same strip, and the equivalent one in the buff-bar hover box, to any mod: hand the engine an item id or a modData key, say which icon and which text each row carries, and it draws them with vanilla's exact geometry. The engine draws only. It never interprets what your rows mean, and your item names, stat concepts and colours never enter it.
[b]World drawing for pieces that stand on the ground (3.1.0 – 3.3.4).[/b] A multi-tile big craftable and a piece of furniture both get drawn by the engine rather than by vanilla's single-cell path: front width, side depth and visual height come from what the item declares, the art is fitted into that footprint without ever being stretched, cropped or rotated, and a tall piece fades while it hides the player. Since 3.3.4 a ground piece and a craftable share one implementation, so the two cannot drift apart — a 2×3 table and a 2×2 machine obey the same geometry.
[b]One more thing (3.3.0): it holds up outside its own drawing.[/b] Every other mod that draws an item icon the vanilla way — gift bubbles, crop bubbles, small icons inside third-party tooltips — keeps using vanilla's "16px cell × 4" while the engine now hands out the whole HD image. HDCore catches that at the lowest draw layer and re-fits it, so an HD icon lands in a bubble at exactly vanilla's size. No mod has to know HDCore exists.
Nothing is taken over unless a mod explicitly asks for it. HDCore never edits assets on disk and never writes to your save: the only load-time changes are in memory, for textures and prices a mod has registered.



[b]Installation instructions[/b]
[list=1]
[*]Install SMAPI 4.0.0 or later.[/*]
[*]Download and unzip HDCore.[/*]
[*]Put the "HDCore" folder into your "Stardew Valley/Mods" folder.[/*]
[*]Launch the game through SMAPI. HDCore logs a "Mounted: item icons…" line once the icon engine is live. The log follows your game language, so the wording matches it.
[/*]
[/list][b]Uninstalling:[/b] delete the "HDCore" folder. Mods that shipped HD icons fall back to vanilla drawing, registered prices return to their original values, the stats panel disappears, and your save is untouched — this mod writes no save data, adds no items and changes no recipes.


[b]Main features[/b]
[b]Icons[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Full-resolution icons, same footprint[/b] — registered textures are drawn from the whole image and scaled into a fixed 64px cell, so your grid layout never changes.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Tilesheets[/b] — a mod can declare an atlas and its cell size, and each item then draws the single cell its "SpriteIndex" points at. Cell size is always declared, never inferred: a 256×256 sheet can be 16px cells or 64px cells, and guessing wrong would squash the whole atlas into one icon. Undeclared atlases keep vanilla slicing.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Registration is the only test (3.3.1)[/b] — a texture is taken over exactly when some registered item references it. The engine walks the item registry (objects, weapons, boots, hats, shirts, pants, furniture, trinkets) and treats the item data itself as the declaration: an unreferenced texture is never touched however large it is, and a referenced 16×16 texture is taken over and comes out pixel-identical to vanilla. There is no size threshold; smaller art simply shows its [b]complete[/b] image instead of the top-left 16×16, and that is an upscale band — whole, not sharper. "RegisterWithMinSize" survives only so older call sites keep working.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Non-square art[/b] — a mod can opt in to padding: the texture is centred and its canvas squared at load time, with no resampling, and then travels the exact same square path. Portrait-shaped art stops rendering as just its top-left corner.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Buff icons[/b] — buff textures can mark themselves for whole-image display even when they are not asset-path textures, which is what custom-loaded buff icons need.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Furniture, weapons, big craftables[/b] — furniture [b]menu/shop icons[/b] fit "longest edge = 64px" (whole image, proportionally scaled — the path non-square dedicated textures such as wall paintings and standing statues travel), and furniture [b]world drawing[/b] has its own family handling since 3.3.2 (see the furniture group below); weapons keep a downscaled copy for the 4× held/swing path while the HD original is used in menus; square big-craftable icons are drawn as a one-cell-wide square anchored to the bottom of their footprint instead of being stretched by the vanilla 1:2 target rectangle.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Every draw site, one rule[/b] — inventory, shops, crafting menu, BetterCrafting grid, buff bar, held items and dropped-item debris all share the same scaling, so HD icons never turn into 4× giants in the world — and the toolbar keeps them centred at its own 0.8/0.9 scale instead of nudging them up-left (3.2.0). Bubbles and third-party tooltips are covered too, without those mods changing anything (3.3.0).[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Large textures[/b] — only square item textures above 1024×1024 are area-averaged down to 1024 at load; anything smaller stays native.[/*]
[/list][b]Multi-tile big craftables (3.1.0)[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Declared, not guessed[/b] — a declared craftable can fill a real multi-tile footprint instead of a single cell. Three numbers describe it: front width makes the texture's horizontal edge exactly fill N tiles (a 128px texture at 2 tiles is drawn at 128px, not stretched); side depth sets how many tiles the object occupies towards +Y and is completely unrelated to the art's aspect ratio; visual height defaults to the aspect-ratio floor, rounded up, and extra height is transparent space at the top, never a stretch.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Real footprint, both directions[/b] — a declared craftable blocks placement on every tile it covers, and ordinary items can no longer be dropped into those tiles. A footprint is what you declared; the art is fitted into it, never the other way round.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]The whole footprint behaves like the main tile (3.2.0)[/b] — collision, right-click interaction, harvesting, pickup and axe / pickaxe / hoe removal all work on every covered tile, not just the one tile that carries the object. Placing a 2×1 machine means you no longer have to hunt for the "real" half before clicking it.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Occlusion fade, with a threshold[/b] — using the same mechanism as vanilla trees, a declared craftable fades smoothly to 50% alpha while the player is behind it and recovers afterwards. It only applies when the computed visual height is 2 tiles or more: a one-tile-tall object can't hide anyone, and fading it would just look like unfinished art.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Whole-image rects everywhere (3.2.1)[/b] — interfaces that don't call the menu draw path but take "item texture + source rect" and paint it themselves (recipe and product mini icons, drop lists, third-party info panels) now receive the full image instead of the top-left corner.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]No code required[/b] — the same declaration is one custom field on the "Data/BigCraftables" entry ("ParadoxQED.HDCore.Layout": "2x1" or "2x1x3"), so a Content Patcher pack gets multi-tile craftables without shipping a DLL. A layout declaration also implies whole-image menu icons, so no separate icon flag is needed.[/*]
[/list][b]Furniture in the world (3.3.2 – 3.3.4)[/b]
[list]
[*][b]One geometry, three families[/b] — furniture front width comes from the "tileSize" the piece declares in "Data/Furniture"; scale = front width × 64 / texture width; visual height is derived from the front width; the bottom edge sits on the footprint bottom, the width is filled exactly and nothing is ever stretched, cropped or rotated.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Ground pieces[/b] (tables, cabinets, standing statues, relics) declare both a front width and a side depth, and fade while they hide the player once their computed visual height reaches 2 tiles — the same smoothed fade multi-tile craftables use. A one-tile-tall piece never fades, because it cannot hide anyone.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Wall pieces[/b] (paintings, windows, sconces, trophies) declare only a front width and derive their visual height from it. They never fade: the player is always in front of them.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Rugs[/b] declare only a front width and derive their side depth from it (front width × texture height / texture width). They lie flat on the floor at the lowest draw depth and never fade. [/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]No extra registration for the family[/b] — the family is item 2 ("type") of "Data/Furniture": painting, window, rug, decor and so on, which the mod already wrote when it created the piece. The engine reads it instead of guessing. Only when that type contradicts how the piece is actually placed (a rug authored as "decor", a wall display authored as a table piece) is an explicit override needed: "DeclareFurnitureFamily(modUniqueId, itemId, "ground" | "wall" | "rug")".[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]One implementation with big craftables (3.3.4)[/b] — a ground piece and a multi-tile craftable have identical geometry, so scale, anchor and the occlusion fade live in a single shared module. Output is pixel-identical to 3.3.3; the point is that the two paths can no longer disagree.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]No more half-size, floating furniture (3.3.2)[/b] — a piece whose texture already matches its declaration is left to the vanilla 4× draw, pixel for pixel; the third-party draw fallback just skips the furniture's own rectangle, which is what used to halve relics and trophies while their position stayed at 4× and left them hovering above the floor.[/*]
[/list][b]Auto-pricing[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Vanilla-calibrated food prices[/b] — price = category coefficient × edibility + 50 × buff points (floor 20G). The nine coefficients are medians regressed from vanilla food pricing; uncategorised food is refused, not guessed.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Ring-ladder accessories[/b] — vanilla-equivalent stat dimensions (attack, weapon speed, speed, crit chance/power, knockback, defense, immunity, luck, magnet, light, skill levels) are weighted with unit prices measured from vanilla gem rings, then snapped to the vanilla price ladder (100 → 10000, then +2500 per step).[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Recipes priced by the target[/b] — a recipe or scroll costs 1/10 of the target item's shop price, matching how vanilla cooking recipes sit under their dish.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Weapons by the vanilla formula[/b] — the engine computes the item level from the weapon's own damage/speed/crit fields, so shop price = level × 100 with no manual level entry.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Special effects stay with the mod[/b] — a mod's signature mechanics are converted to vanilla-equivalent numbers plus a special tier (minor ≥ 1500G, major ≥ 2000G) before submission; the engine never invents prices for effects it cannot measure.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Timing-safe[/b] — prices are edited during asset loading, after Content Patcher patches. Systems that read prices at runtime (for example stats derived from price) always see the final value; there is no old-price/new-price mismatch.[/*]
[/list][b]Stats panel[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Nine built-in rows[/b] — health, stamina, defense, immunity, speed, damage, crit chance, weapon speed and fishing. Fishing shows extra levels from buffs only, not your own skill.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Zero reporting required[/b] — the panel reads the game's buff-effect aggregate. Vanilla gear, food and festival dishes, plus any mod that writes into that aggregate, appear automatically. The engine does not need to know a mod's name.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Only generic bonuses[/b] — class-specific multipliers that never reach the global total are deliberately not shown; the panel will not do arithmetic on behalf of someone else's progression system.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Controls[/b] — show/hide with numpad minus by default. Dragging is off by default; when enabled, hold left mouse to move the panel and its position is saved as screen ratios. Zero-value rows can be hidden, and the text can be scaled.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Vanilla bar takeover (optional)[/b] — hide the vanilla health and stamina bars and render both as progress rows inside the panel. Only the bar segment of the HUD is patched; the clock, toolbar, buff bar and forage arrows are untouched, and the feature unloads itself rather than crash if the game's method no longer matches.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Mod config menu[/b] — with Generic Mod Config Menu installed you get a "Stats panel" page for all of the above. Without it the page is skipped silently and editing "config.json" works the same way.[/*]
[/list][b]Tooltip icon rows (3.2.0)[/b]
[list]
[*][b]The vanilla enchantment slot, opened up[/b] — rows are drawn exactly where vanilla puts its own special-icon lines: after an item's description, stat lines and enchantment, before the bottom edge. Weapons, rings, tools, accessories and big craftables all reach the same strip, because the engine hooks all three tooltip paths the game uses rather than only the weapon one. The strip is reserved at exactly vanilla height, so a tooltip with rows is not a few pixels taller than one without (3.2.2).[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Two surfaces[/b] — item tooltips, and the hover box over your buff bar. A buff row can read its number straight from the buff's own effects at draw time, so nothing goes stale when a buff is rebuilt every second.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]You supply the meaning[/b] — the engine knows nothing about your items, your stats or your names. Which id gets which rows, which texture rect the icon comes from, what the text says, what colour it is — all of it arrives as data, and every label you pass in is an already-localised string.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Rows that follow item state[/b] — besides matching by item id, a mod can match on a modData key and supply one row set per value. That covers gear whose display depends on what it has been upgraded, rolled or enchanted into, without the mod hooking the draw call itself. It also guarantees the space-reservation pass and the draw pass see the same value.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Four icon sources[/b] — vanilla sprite slices, slices of any registered texture, and engine-drawn shapes (star, dot, square) for cases where an arbitrary tint is needed. The shapes are pure white on purpose: vanilla's special icons carry their own colours, so tinting those gives muddy results.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Hover bodies[/b] — any row can carry its own explanation, shown in a native tooltip box while the cursor is over it. A two-word label does not have to explain itself in the row.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Zero contact by default[/b] — no registration, no rows. Each hook is wrapped individually, so a failure disables the rows and leaves the vanilla tooltip untouched.[/*]
[/list][b]For other mods[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Hosted rows and bars[/b] — a mod can push a labelled row or a progress bar into the panel and it follows the panel's scale, visibility and drag. Labels and values are already-localised strings supplied by the caller, so no foreign terminology ends up inside the engine.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Self-drawn gauges[/b] — a mod with its own art can ask for a slot and get a non-overlapping x. Mods that sit left of the vanilla bars are laid out right-to-left by priority and never collide; a slot not refreshed for one second is released and neighbours close the gap.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Bubbles and tooltips handled for you (3.3.0)[/b] — if your mod draws an item icon by taking the item's texture and source rect and painting it at a vanilla cell multiplier, the engine re-fits that draw to vanilla size automatically. Your code stays as it is; the only trace is a log line naming the texture.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Fail-safe by design[/b] — every patch is wrapped individually, so one failed hook disables only that path and never interrupts the game. Unregistered mods, undeclared atlases, 16×16 legacy art and UI textures are never touched.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Requirements[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Stardew Valley 1.6+[/b][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]SMAPI 4.0.0+[/b] (required)[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b] (optional) — adds an in-game page for the stats panel; without it "config.json" works the same.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]BetterCrafting[/b] (optional) — its recipe grid is scaled automatically, and since 3.3.5 hovering a recipe grows the icon by the same proportion vanilla art grows instead of by a fixed scale delta. HDCore never references its assembly directly, so it is skipped silently when absent.
[/*]
[/list][b]For mod authors[/b]
HDCore is a framework; nothing is taken over automatically. To have your icons handled:

[list=1]
[*]Declare the dependency in your "manifest.json", with the minimum version matching the API you actually call. The entry reads: "Dependencies": [ { "UniqueID": "ParadoxQED.HDCore", "MinimumVersion": "3.2.0", "IsRequired": true } ]Do not declare a lower version than the methods you use — SMAPI's API proxy resolves members by name, so calling a newer method against an older build fails at runtime instead of at load.[/*]
[*]Declare a matching interface in your own source. You do [b]not[/b] need to reference "HDCore.dll" — SMAPI proxies the API by member name. Only the members you actually call have to be present:
Properties: "IsApplied", "IconSize", "IndexedTextures", "StatsHudEnabled", "IconRowsHooked".Icons: "Register(modUniqueId, textureNamePatterns)", "RegisterWithMinSize(modUniqueId, textureNamePatterns, minSize)", "RegisterSheets(modUniqueId, textureNamePatterns, cellSize)", "RegisterPadded(modUniqueId, textureNamePatterns, minSize)", "RegisterHatHd(modUniqueId, hatHdTextures)".Stats panel: "SetHudRow(modUniqueId, key, label, value, order, warning)", "SetHudBar(modUniqueId, key, label, text, ratio, order, warning, colorRgb)", "ClearHudRow(modUniqueId, key)", "ClearHudRows(modUniqueId)", "SetHudSlot(modUniqueId, key, width, priority)", "GetHudSlotX(modUniqueId, key)".Pricing (3.0.0+): "RegisterPricing(modUniqueId, itemsJson)", "UnregisterPricing(modUniqueId)", "GetAutoPrice(itemId)".Big-craftable layouts (3.1.0+): "DeclareBigCraftableLayout(modUniqueId, itemId, frontTiles, sideTiles, visualHeight)", "UnregisterBigCraftableLayout(modUniqueId)".Furniture family override (3.3.3+, optional): "DeclareFurnitureFamily(modUniqueId, itemId, family)" where family is "ground", "wall" or "rug", and "UnregisterFurnitureFamily(modUniqueId)". Not needed when the "type" field of "Data/Furniture" already matches the real placement.Tooltip icon rows (3.2.0+): "RegisterItemIconRows(modUniqueId, rulesJson)", "RegisterBuffIconRows(modUniqueId, rulesJson)", "RegisterModDataIconRows(modUniqueId, rulesJson)", "ClearIconRows(modUniqueId)".Every method returns bool except the four properties (bool and int) and "GetHudSlotX", which returns int.[/*]
[*]Register from "GameLaunched" — querying the API earlier returns null. Ask "Helper.ModRegistry.GetApi" for your interface type with the ID "ParadoxQED.HDCore", then call "Register" with your manifest UniqueID and the texture path prefixes you want handled.[/*]
[/list]Pricing entry format — each entry in "itemsJson" declares one item:
[list]
[*]"Id" (required), "Asset" ("Objects" / "Weapons" / "Boots" / "Shirts" / "Pants"), "Kind" ("weapon" / "accessory" / "food").[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]"Kind":"weapon" — supply nothing else; the engine reads the weapon's own stats and applies the vanilla level formula.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]"Kind":"accessory" — "Stats" holds vanilla-equivalent dimensions: "attackPct", "wspeedPct", "speedPct", "critChancePct", "critPowerPct", "knockbackPct" (percent), "defense", "immunity", "luck", "skillPoints" (points), "magnetPx", "light" (pixels / radius); "SpecialTier" 0 = pure stats, 1 = minor special (floor 1500G), 2 = major special (floor 2000G).[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]"Kind":"food" — "Group" is one of "fish", "milk", "egg", "artisan", "vegetable", "fruit", "forage", "flower", "dish"; "Edibility" defaults to the asset's own value; "Buff" holds vanilla BuffEffects-style keys ("attack", "defense", "speed", "luck", "immunity", "maxstamina", "magnet", skills, percentages…) in vanilla units. Uncategorised food is refused and keeps its original price.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]"RecipeFor" — this entry is the target item's recipe; its shop price becomes 1/10 of the target's.[/*]
[/list]Example entries for "itemsJson" (one JSON object per registered item):
[list]
[*]{"Id": "MyMod_MagicSword", "Asset": "Weapons", "Kind": "weapon"}[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]{"Id": "MyMod_RubyRing", "Asset": "Objects", "Kind": "accessory", "Stats": {"attackPct": 10}, "SpecialTier": 0}[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]{"Id": "MyMod_FishPie", "Asset": "Objects", "Kind": "food", "Group": "dish", "Buff": {"attack": 3, "maxstamina": 40}}[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]{"Id": "MyMod_FishPieRecipe", "Asset": "Objects", "Kind": "food", "RecipeFor": "MyMod_FishPie"}[/*]
[/list]Big-craftable layout notes (3.1.0):
[list]
[*]"frontTiles" (≥1): the texture's horizontal edge exactly fills this many tiles — draw width = frontTiles × 64, scale = frontTiles × 64 / texture width, independent of texture resolution.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]"sideTiles" (≥1): tiles occupied towards +Y (collision depth); completely unrelated to the art's aspect ratio.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]"visualHeight": pass 0 to let the engine pick the legal floor = ceil(texture height × scale / 64). A larger integer is respected and shows as transparent space at the top; a smaller one is raised to the floor. The art is never stretched.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]The CP equivalent is "CustomFields": {"ParadoxQED.HDCore.Layout": "2x1"} or "2x1x3" on the "Data/BigCraftables" entry. A layout declaration also implies whole-image icons — no separate icon flag needed.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Declared craftables get real multi-tile collision, placement blocking in both directions, whole-footprint interaction (right-click, harvest, pickup, axe / pickaxe / hoe) and an occlusion fade while the player is behind them. The fade only switches on when the computed visual height reaches 2 tiles; shorter objects are left alone.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Visual height is computed, never assumed: the floor comes from the texture's own height, so replacing the art changes it. Pass an explicit "visualHeight" when the result has to stay fixed across art revisions.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]The extra tiles carry no object of their own, so anything that looks an object up by tile coordinate finds only the main tile — which is exactly why the engine redirects interaction itself. A player already standing inside a covered tile is let through rather than trapped, so nobody gets stuck after loading an old save.[/*]
[/list]Tooltip icon row notes (3.2.0):
[list]
[*]"rulesJson" is an array, one entry per matcher. Item rules use "ItemId" (exact) or "ItemIdPrefix"; buff rules use "BuffId" / "BuffIdPrefix"; modData rules use "Key" plus a "Cases" table mapping each value to its own row array.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]"Order" sorts rule groups against each other (smaller first), so two matchers that both hit the same item combine in the order you expect.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]A row carries "Text" [b]or[/b] "Stat". "Stat" is "defense" or "immunity" and the engine builds the label from the game's own strings; "Text" is a finished, already-localised string. On top of that: "Value", "Suffix", "Icon", "IconTint", "TextTint", "Scale" (default 4), "Tip". [/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Icon syntax: "vanilla:x,y,w,h" (Game1.mouseCursors), "vanilla2:x,y,w,h" (mouseCursors_1_6), "asset:assetName|0,0,64,64" (any texture; SMAPI asset name without extension; rect optional, omit it for the whole image), "shape:star|dot|square".[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Buff rules only: "NameOnlyBody" trims the vanilla body to "name + separator + description"; "DropSourceLine" drops the "Source:" line.[/*]
[/list]Example entries for "rulesJson":
[list]
[*]{"ItemId": "MyMod_Charm", "Order": 100, "Rows": [{"Stat": "defense", "Value": 3, "Icon": "vanilla:110,428,10,10"}, {"Text": "Resonance", "Icon": "shape:star", "IconTint": "#9696FF", "TextTint": "#9696FF", "Tip": "Resonance: +5% attack on every third hit."}]}[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]{"Key": "MyMod/Upgrade", "Order": 200, "Cases": {"tier1": [{"Text": "Tier I", "Icon": "shape:dot", "IconTint": "#9696FF"}], "tier2": [{"Text": "Tier II", "Icon": "shape:dot", "IconTint": "#96FF96"}]}}[/*]
[/list]Notes that save time:
[list]
[*]Registration is rejected when the dependency is not declared in your manifest. Methods are deliberately [b]not[/b] overloaded — SMAPI maps by method name, so distinct names avoid ambiguity.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Convert your mod's signature effects into vanilla-equivalent numbers [b]before[/b] submitting: the engine only understands vanilla units, and a tier flag carries what the numbers cannot (minor special ≥ 1500G, major special ≥ 2000G).[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Auto-pricing edits happen at asset-load time (after Content Patcher), so any runtime system that reads prices — including ones that derive their own values from price — always sees the final value.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Author your icons as [b]square, at least 64×64[/b] (68, 72, 96, 128, 288 all work; the engine scales by actual edge). If the source art is rectangular, either pad the short edge up to the long one in the PNG, or leave the PNG alone and call "RegisterPadded" — never stretch it.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Do [b]not[/b] call "RegisterPadded" on furniture textures that are also placed in the world: since 3.3.2 furniture world drawing follows "whole image + declared front width", so padding the canvas changes the on-world size and position. Icons are fine; placement is not.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]HUD rows and bars accept already-localised strings; you supply every language. "ratio" means only used/max, "colorRgb" is 0xRRGGBB with -1 for a red→green gradient, and "order" ascends from the top. Built-in rows occupy 1–70; use 3–9 for resource rows and 100+ for pure info rows.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Pushing the same modUniqueId and key every frame is fine — rows are compared field by field and unchanged values do not re-layout anything.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]In hosted mode, do not draw your own copy as well, or the same bar shows twice. Use "StatsHudEnabled" to decide between "engine draws it" and "I draw it".[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Tooltip icon rows are 48px tall and drawn at vanilla's own offsets. A "Scale" that pushes an icon past 48px overlaps the neighbouring row, so keep icon art at 10×10 or raise "Scale" deliberately.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Icon row registrations [b]accumulate[/b]: calling "RegisterItemIconRows" twice for the same id adds rows instead of replacing them. Use "ClearIconRows" to reset a mod's rows before re-registering.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Probe "IconRowsHooked" before relying on rows. An older engine build lacks the member, and SMAPI's proxy reports a missing member as absent — treat that as "draw it yourself", not as an error.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Do [b]not[/b] express hover growth as a fixed scale delta on top of a fitted scale. 0.1 added to vanilla's fitted 4.0 is a 2.5% pop; the same 0.1 added to a whole image fitted at 0.062 is a 161% jump. Make the delta proportional to the fitted scale. HDCore already converts this for its own rectangles, but any UI that mixes whole images with fixed deltas hits the same arithmetic.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]If your mod draws an item icon by sampling "GetTexture()" plus "GetSourceRect()" and painting it yourself, you do [b]not[/b] need to change anything: the engine re-fits that draw to vanilla size automatically. If you would rather control it, draw the icon yourself via "drawInMenu" and the engine's menu path takes over cleanly.[/*]
[/list]


[b]Shout outs[/b]
[list]
[*]The Stardew Valley modding community and the SMAPI team, for an API that makes this kind of surgical draw-path change possible.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Everyone who reported blurry or oversized icons — those reports shaped the 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 fixes, and the 2.x work that followed.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Players who kept reporting "the icon in this bubble is enormous" — that turned into 3.3.0, which fixes all such bubbles at once instead of one mod at a time.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Players who caught an icon exploding under the cursor in a crafting grid — the fixed-delta hover bug behind it became 3.3.5.[/*]
[/list]

Manifest.Name: HD 图标引擎 (HDCore)
Manifest.Description: 高清物品图标引擎：贴图整图取样 + 屏幕上恒定 64px + 制作界面（含 BetterCrafting）同步缩放。接管的唯一判据是「这张贴图被某个已注册物品引用」——引擎从物品注册表反推，物品数据本身就是声明：没被任何物品引用的贴图永不接管，被引用的就一定会接管，尺寸不做任何要求（16×16 也接管，换算后与原版逐像素一致）。另两条只是几何前提：贴图必须方形、SpriteIndex = 0。图集格子边长必须显式声明（RegisterSheets），绝不从尺寸反推。2.1 起 RegisterPadded 支持非方形素材：加载期把短边居中、两边扩画布补成正方形，之后按方形口径接管（同样必须显式声明）。1.2.0：修正建造物世界绘制的 1:2 拉伸。1.2.1：加载降采样阈值 256 → 1024。 2.2.0：buff 栏图标支持「模组自证」——模组可在 buff.customFields["ParadoxQED.HDCore.BuffIcon"]="1" 声明该 buff 图标为 HD 整图，引擎按整图铺 64px（原先仅认「注册范围内、方形 ≥64」，自定义资产键与 17~63 素材无法命中）。 2.3.0：新增常驻属性面板——把「防御 / 免疫 / 移速 / 伤害 / 暴击 / 钓鱼」画在屏幕上，数值直接取游戏已算好的总账（Farmer.buffs 的 BuffEffects 汇总 + 原版战斗职业分支 + 书本移速），因此原版鞋子/戒指/食物/节日料理与任何走 BuffEffects 的模组加成都自动计入，无需注册；模组可通过 SetHudRow 往面板下方推自定义行（标签与数值的多语言由模组自己提供，引擎不解释其含义）。 2.4.0：面板加入「钓鱼加成」（BuffManager.FishingLevel 的额外等级）；新增 GMCM 配置页（显示开关 / 显隐按键 / 隐藏零值行），显隐按键默认小键盘减号（SButton.Subtract），未装 GMCM 时静默跳过、config.json 手动改同样生效。 2.5.0：面板加入「武器速度」（BuffManager.WeaponSpeedMultiplier——原版唯一的攻速字段，作用点是 MeleeWeapon.swipeSpeed 挥砍动画与弹弓初速，弹幕速度不在这一行），并把开关做进 GMCM：显示面板、显隐按键（默认小键盘减号）、拖动调整位置、隐藏零值行；拖动开启时按住左键可把面板拖到任意位置，松手把位置按比例写回 config.json。 2.6.0：面板支持「带进度条的数值行」（SetHudBar，比例与颜色由接入方给），并可接管原版血量/精力条——开启后把两根条藏起来、在面板里画成带进度条的行（只动 Game1.drawHUD 里双条那一段，时钟/工具栏/buff 栏/觅食指引不受影响；特征失配时自动放弃，不会崩）。新增槽位仲裁 SetHudSlot/GetHudSlotX，多个模组贴原版状态条左侧时自动排开不重叠。 2.7.0：建造物（bigCraftables）改为**声明制** —— 只有模组显式声明的建造物才按整图绘制（菜单/商店铺满一格、世界与放置预览一格宽底贴格底）。两条等价通道：Data/BigCraftables 条目的 CustomFields["ParadoxQED.HDCore.Icon"]="BigCraftable"（CP 首选），或 API DeclareBigCraftableIcons(mod, ids)。未声明的走原版 16×32。旧版对「尚未采用声明制的接入方」保留过「方形 ≥64 自动接管」的兼容层，3.3.1 已删除：没声明就不接管。 3.0.0 新增注册制自动定价引擎：只有模组显式调 RegisterPricing 声明的物品才会被接管价格；引擎按原版口径计算（武器等级公式 / 饰品位阶 / 食性系数），自动给出玩家出售所得、商店定价（2×直售）与配方定价（直售商店价 1/10）。零注册零接触。 3.1.0 新增建造物多格布局声明：CustomFields["ParadoxQED.HDCore.Layout"]="正面x侧面[视觉高度]" 或 API DeclareBigCraftableLayout —— 正面边长严格对应贴图横向边（占满 N 格），侧面边长决定碰撞深度，视觉高度缺省按长宽比取合法整数（多出的高度是顶部透明占位，绝不拉伸），并带遮挡半透明。未声明的一律走原版 1×1。 3.2.0 新增提示框图标行引擎：把「小图标 + 一段文字」画进原版给特殊图标留的位置（物品提示框的描述/属性/附魔之后、buff 栏悬停框的正文之后），几何逐像素对齐原版。引擎只负责绘制，不解释任何内容模组的术语——哪件物品/哪个 buff 出哪几行、图标取自哪张图的哪个矩形、文字与颜色，全部由接入方通过 RegisterItemIconRows / RegisterBuffIconRows / RegisterModDataIconRows 提交；图标支持原版切片、任意资产切片与引擎自绘形状（star/dot/square，可染任意色）。零注册时对原版零接触。 3.2.1：修正建造物取图矩形——BigCraftableDataDefinition.GetSourceRect 之前漏挂补丁，凡是按物品矩形取样、不走 drawInMenu 的界面（LookupAnything 的配方/产物小图标、掉落列表…）建造物只显示整图左上角；现按声明制返回整图。 3.2.2：提示框图标行不再额外多留 6px 底部空隙——多留会让带图标行的物品「售价」那一段比没有图标行的物品高 6px，玩家会当成价签框变高；行内图标本来就画在行间余量里，不会越界。 3.3.0：第三方绘制兜底——引擎把物品的取图矩形改成整图后，别处仍按原版「16px 单元格 × 4」去画的代码（送礼提示气泡、作物气泡、第三方提示框里的小图标…）会把图标放大成 4 格大小的巨型贴图。引擎现在在 SpriteBatch.Draw 这一层兜底：矩形确实是引擎发出去的、且请求宽度超过 1.5 格时，把倍率折回「16 × 调用方倍率」、origin 同比换算，画出来与原版 16×16 的位置尺寸完全一致——任何模组都不需要适配，引擎自己的绘制整段绕开这一层。 3.3.1：引擎内所有靠尺寸猜的判断全部改成注册制——接管的唯一判据是「这张贴图被某个已注册物品引用」（从物品注册表反推，尺寸不做任何要求），剩下只有方形与 SpriteIndex=0 两条几何前提；建造物删掉「方形 ≥64 自动接管」兼容层，一律声明制；补齐家具与饰品的取图矩形接管（FurnitureDataDefinition / TrinketDataDefinition 之前漏挂），第三方气泡里的圣物、纪念章、饰品图标不再只显示整图左上角；顺带去掉每帧需要遍历的尺寸判定，改为无锁集合查。 3.3.2：家具世界绘制分三族适配 —— 地面型（圣物、立像、桌椅柜）、挂墙型（壁画、窗、壁灯、纪念章）、地毯型，三族共用同一条几何：正面边长取自家具自己的 Data/Furniture 声明（tileSize 第一项），缩放 = 正面×64 / 贴图宽，视觉高度 = ceil(贴图高×缩放/64)，底边贴占格底边，只在层深上分叉（地毯最低、挂墙在人物之后、地面常规）。同时修正 3.3.0 兜底缩放误伤家具本体的问题：家具本体那一块源矩形由 Furniture.draw 自己声明，兜底一律放行 —— 之前它被当成「16px 单元格」折半，导致圣物、纪念章缩成一半并悬在半空。贴图与声明一致时仍走原版 4×（逐像素不变），贴图大于声明时按整图接管，不旋转、不拉伸、不缩放素材。 3.3.3：家具三族的语义补齐（此前只修了「兜底折半导致缩成一半并悬空」那一个 bug）。地面型按「正面边长 + 侧面边长」占格，视觉高度由正面边长算出，视觉高度 ≥ 2 格时挡住玩家会半透明（与多格建造物共用同一套平滑实现）；挂墙型只有正面边长，视觉高度同样由正面边长算出，玩家永远在它前面，不做半透明；地毯型只有正面边长，侧面边长由正面边长推出（round(正面 × 贴图高 / 贴图宽)），平铺在地板上，不做半透明。族别不需要模组额外注明：它就是 Data/Furniture 第 2 项的 type（painting / window / rug / decor…），模组创建家具时已经写了；只有类型写法与摆放语义不一致时，才用新增的 DeclareFurnitureFamily(modId, itemId, ground|wall|rug) 覆盖。 3.3.4：把「站在地面上的东西」的世界绘制抽成共用几何层 —— 多格建造物与地面型家具现在走同一份代码：横向铺满（缩放 = 正面×64 / 贴图宽）、底边贴占格底边、视觉高度由正面边长算出、遮挡半透明与「视觉高度 ≥ 2 格」闸门共用一处实现。行为与 3.3.3 逐像素一致，纯粹消掉两套并行公式。不共用的三件事仍然是分开的：声明来源（建造物要显式布局，家具读 tileSize）、占格与交互补丁（家具的原版 boundingBox 本来就是多格）、层深（建造物要插进物体层，家具三族各有口径）。 3.3.5：修正 BetterCrafting 制作界面里鼠标悬停时图标异常放大。它的悬停放大是「固定倍率增量」——对原版 16×16 素材可忽略（4.0 → 4.1），但对整图建造物（例：680×1028 的贴图在 64px 格里适配倍率只有 0.062）加上 0.1 就是画成 167px、2.6 倍。补丁只在这个绘制方法执行期间把组件倍率临时换算成比例值，让悬停放大比例与原版一致，返回后立刻还原；只处理源矩形由本引擎发布的绘制，BetterCrafting 缺席或改实现时自动跳过。
